# [E7 — Pesticides and degradation products](../openproblems/E7.md "Pesticides and degradation products")

*Generated by `scripts/pages/openproblem_e7.py` from the draft as committed at `c601feb`. Counts of files held in this repository are read live. Counts that session made from external sources or from one-off runs are quotations of that commit - what the draft reported, shown as such, not re-derived by the build.*


**Missing: measurement.** The quantity the hypothesis is about is not recorded in this
archive at any density, in any matrix, at any station. [E7](../openproblems/E7.md "Pesticides and degradation products") is therefore **unscoreable, not
refuted** — an absent dimension (error class 6), not a null result.

## What a test would need, and which side is empty

[E7](../openproblems/E7.md "Pesticides and degradation products") says agricultural pesticides reach the sea and act on non-target organisms, and that
they are collinear with nitrogen because the same farming produces both. Discriminating
it needs three things at shared positions: (a) a concentration of at least one **named**
active substance or degradation product in water, sediment or biota; (b) a fauna or
algal response; (c) a nutrient-load covariate to hold fixed. (c) is abundant here. (b)
exists in ODA `Bundfauna`, not yet fetched. **(a) does not exist in anything held.**

## What is actually here — counted

- `docs/data/areas/stations_series.json` — **[679,422](../SOURCES.md#F-b61d7944ec) station-months**, [1,415](../SOURCES.md#F-fff0060a3d) stations,
  [564](../SOURCES.md#F-008df4b99b) monthly slots from 1980, across **[9](../SOURCES.md#F-81bea72caf) variables**: fluorescence, oxygen and oxygen
  saturation (bed and surface), salinity and temperature (bed and surface). **No
  toxicant variable of any kind.** Near-bed oxygen alone is **[76,980](../SOURCES.md#F-a95c664ddf) station-months over
  [1,327](../SOURCES.md#F-a053d110be) stations**, [348](../SOURCES.md#F-a18d57e4e7) of them with ≥[60](../SOURCES.md#F-df8fed9880) months and [231](../SOURCES.md#F-a3a658247b) with ≥[120](../SOURCES.md#F-aac821b391) — the response-side
  record is dense; the exposure side has no column to sit in.
- `data/raw/oda/stations.csv` — the ODA register: [798,574](../SOURCES.md#F-84ce7a3cde) rows, **[6,288](../SOURCES.md#F-53e5dbbec4) distinct marine
  observation sites** (`Hav` [798,324](../SOURCES.md#F-5aa80fe61a) rows, `Havn` [201](../SOURCES.md#F-2ee8b4c5e1), `Punkt i fjord` [49](../SOURCES.md#F-45cbc05f9a)).
- `data/raw/oda/ctd.csv.gz` — **[53,712,716](../SOURCES.md#F-db8f674bc0) measurements** scanned in full; the `Parameter` column takes **[17](../SOURCES.md#F-0a044f4564) distinct named values**: Temperatur, Salinitet, Oxygen indhold, Fluorescens, Oxygenmætning, Lysdæmpning, Konduktivitet, Vægtfylde, Turbiditet, FDOM, Photometer måling, Photometer reference, pH, Strømhastighed, Strømretning, Farvestof, Dihydrogensulfid ([2,601](../SOURCES.md#F-67c457d6d9) rows), plus [3,381](../SOURCES.md#F-e33ac37e24) blank. **Not one is a pesticide, a degradation product, or any organic contaminant.**
- `data/raw/geus/` holds only `seabed_sediment_dk.gpkg` and `marta_sedimentproever.geojson`
  — a sediment **map** and raw-material samples. There is **no Jupiter groundwater
  chemistry** here; the three groundwater layers in `data/raw/` are water levels ([419](../SOURCES.md#F-04e0683b55)),
  potentiometric contours ([138](../SOURCES.md#F-899f3c6ba5)) and depth-to-table polygons ([2,087](../SOURCES.md#F-09ead7574c)), carrying no analyte.
  The groundwater route to a land-side pesticide series is not present in this archive.
- No pesticide **sales or usage** series either: keyword search over `docs/DATA_QUEUE.md`
  ([145](../SOURCES.md#F-5164381ffc) sources) and `data/raw/` returns no *bekæmpelsesmiddelstatistik*,
  *behandlingshyppighed* or equivalent. Such statistics are published nationally; that is
  general knowledge and is **not verified from anything in this repository**.

## The only layer in the archive that mentions pollutants at all

`data/raw/national/sw_mfs_tilstand.geojson` — **[256](../SOURCES.md#F-2e0664e8b7) points, none of them marine**: [152](../SOURCES.md#F-e8df38bf02)
`DKLAKE`, [104](../SOURCES.md#F-886deb6674) `DKRIVER`. Matrices flagged: biota [253](../SOURCES.md#F-4d1a1b05ed), water [174](../SOURCES.md#F-08fa672da8), **sediment [5](../SOURCES.md#F-fad92131f2)**, nothing [3](../SOURCES.md#F-37d1c997e7).
What each point carries is `qecode = "QE3-3 - River Basin Specific Pollutants"` for all
[256](../SOURCES.md#F-2e0664e8b7), `qestatusor = "3"` for all [256](../SOURCES.md#F-2e0664e8b7), `da_oekolog = "2"` for all [256](../SOURCES.md#F-2e0664e8b7), and `aktivstart =
01-01-1999` for all [256](../SOURCES.md#F-2e0664e8b7). **No analyte name, no concentration, no unit, no sampling date.**

- **Class 4, schema conflation.** One quality-element code pools every river-basin-specific
  pollutant — pesticides, metals, everything — into a single column. A pesticide effect
  cannot be separated from a metal one even in principle at this resolution.
- **Class 7, model-as-datum.** The value is a status verdict, and it is invariant across
  all [256](../SOURCES.md#F-2e0664e8b7) points, so it carries zero information for discriminating anything.
- **Class 3 / [7](../SOURCES.md#F-f16a3c5ee7) downstream.** `docs/data/areas/areas.json` marks **[66](../SOURCES.md#F-114148732f) of the [123](../SOURCES.md#F-7c7b52f5f3) marine
  water bodies** as having hazardous-substance observation. That flag is manufactured in
  `scripts/areas.py` by assigning each of these inland points to the *nearest marine water
  body within `MAX_ASSIGN_KM = 20`* — [205](../SOURCES.md#F-18831ce0c1) of the [256](../SOURCES.md#F-2e0664e8b7) were assigned this way. The marine
  toxicant "coverage" in this archive is lake and stream points attributed to the sea by
  proximity. It is not a marine sample, and it is not a pesticide measurement.

## Why *measurement* and not the other two

Not **experiment**: no intervention is required. Ordinary monitoring, of a kind already
run for nutrients, would produce the series.

Not **armchair**: an armchair block means the numbers exist and joining them is merely
too large. Here the join has one side. `docs/DATA_QUEUE.md` does list marine
hazardous-substance topics in ODA that this project holds credentials for — `ODA-MFS-FISK`,
`ODA-MFS-MUSLING`, `ODA-SEDKEMI-MFS` (*Hav / Sedimentkemi / MFS Sporstof*) — and **their
analyte lists have not been verified by anyone here**. That uncertainty is itself the
point: nobody in this project can currently say whether a single marine pesticide
concentration is recorded in Denmark, which is what makes this a measurement question.

**Reclassification test, stated in advance.** If enumeration shows named pesticide or
degradation-product analytes at ≥[20](../SOURCES.md#F-28746c3799) marine stations with ≥[5](../SOURCES.md#F-b0cd2ae20d) years of dated results and a
non-censored fraction above roughly a third, [E7](../openproblems/E7.md "Pesticides and degradation products") moves to **armchair** and this file is
wrong. Anything thinner leaves it here.

## Smallest unblocking thing

1. **Enumerate, do not download.** Run the topic and parameter *metadata* calls already
   implemented in `scripts/fetch_oda.py` (`expand`, `option_list`) against Hav /
   Sedimentkemi / MFS Sporstof, Hav / MFS i biota, and Hav / Vandkemi, and record the
   parameter names and per-parameter station counts. Metadata only, no extract. One
   session. This decides whether [E7](../openproblems/E7.md "Pesticides and degradation products") has an exposure side at all.
2. **If it does not**, the smallest useful addition is one analyte panel bolted onto
   stations that already carry fauna: ~[20](../SOURCES.md#F-547d026796) existing `Bundfauna` stations spanning an
   agricultural gradient, four sampling rounds a year (pre-application, two post, winter),
   sediment plus passive samplers. Three requirements, each of which the existing layer
   violates: **named analytes reported individually, never a "pesticides" sum** (class 4);
   **per-analyte LOD reported with every result**, and chosen below the effect
   concentration for the conserved target rather than wherever the instrument lands; and
   **"< LOD" recorded as censoring with its threshold** (class 2), so a non-detect is
   reportable as a bound instead of silently becoming a zero. Pick the panel by target
   conservation, not market label: a photosystem-II inhibitor plus its degradation product
   (the algae the chlorophyll indicator counts), a neuroactive (copepods), an azole (the
   sterol pathway every eukaryote has), and glyphosate with AMPA.

## What such data would, and would not, license

Even a complete marine pesticide series would **not** license "pesticides did it". [E7](../openproblems/E7.md "Pesticides and degradation products")'s
own prediction is that pesticide and nitrogen load are collinear because one agriculture
produces both, so a concentration series is only discriminating where the two vary
independently — same nutrient load, different pesticide exposure. Whether that contrast
exists anywhere in Danish waters is a second, unanswered measurement question, and it is
worth answering *before* collecting the first series rather than after. What the series
would license immediately is narrower and still worth having: a statement of whether the
exposure is present at concentrations near the effect thresholds of the conserved targets
at all — which at present nobody here can make in either direction.
